title: Longest Mirror Subsequence
statement:
A **subsequence** keeps the letters of a text in their original order but may skip some of them. A **mirror** reads the same forwards and backwards.

Return the length of the longest subsequence of `text` that is a mirror. The letters do not have to be next to each other in `text`.
constraints: text uses only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Skip the `a`: `bbbb` is a mirror of length 4.
`bb` is the longest mirror you can pick.

hints.nudge: Look at the first and the last letter of a stretch of the text. If they are equal, what can you do with them?
hints.pattern: Interval DP: best[i][j] = the answer for the part of the text from position i to position j.
hints.walkthrough: Checking every subsequence takes 2^n steps. Instead define best[i][j] as the answer for text[i..j]. A single letter is a mirror of length 1. If text[i] and text[j] are equal, they can sit at the two ends of a mirror, so the answer is 2 + best[i+1][j-1] (an empty inside counts as 0). If they differ, one of them is not used: take the larger of best[i+1][j] and best[i][j-1]. Fill the table with i going downwards so that the smaller stretches are ready. The answer is best[0][n-1]. O(n^2) time and memory. Another view: the answer equals the longest common subsequence of the text and its reverse.
